listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Noor and Yousef.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Hi Yousef! Good news. I spoke to the principal this morning, and he has agreed to our recycling campaign.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: That is wonderful! I have been worried about the school yard for a long time. At every break time I see rubbish on the ground.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Me too. Plastic bottles are the biggest problem, much bigger than paper bags or food waste. That is why this campaign is so important.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: How long will it last? One week is not enough for students to change their habits.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: I agree. The principal suggested a whole month, but that is too long. Two weeks is better, and he accepted that.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Great. Now we must plan everything carefully. Where shall we put the first bins?

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The main gate is too far from the classes. I think the best place is next to the canteen, because everybody buys drinks there.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Good idea. We will need about ten bins at the start. What about colours? We need different bins for different materials.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Yellow for plastic, green for cans and blue for paper. Many countries use the same colours, so students will understand them quickly.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Perfect. We also need posters to tell everyone about the campaign. They must be colourful and easy to read.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The art club can make them. I asked Ms Maryam yesterday, and she said yes. I wanted the science club first, but they are busy with the science fair.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: What about a prize? Students will work harder if there is something to win. They need a good reason to take part.

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: The class that recycles the most will win a trip to the beach. I thought about a pizza party, but a trip is more exciting.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: Fantastic! The students will love that. Who will take the recycling away?

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: A local company will collect it every Thursday. Not on Sunday, because the school is very busy on that day.

script.speaker: Yousef
script.text: That is very helpful. Then we are ready. Shall we tell the whole school about the campaign in tomorrow's assembly?

script.speaker: Noor
script.text: Yes, let's do that. I will prepare a short speech tonight, and you can bring the posters. I am sure this campaign will make our school cleaner and greener.

items.q: What is the biggest problem in the school yard?
How long will the campaign last?
Where will the first bins be?
Which colour will the paper bins be?
Which club will make the posters?
What will the winning class get?
On which day will a company collect the recycling?

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about the history of Omani sailors and trade.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Welcome, everyone. Today's talk is about Omani sailors and the trade routes of the sea.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Oman has a very long coast, and for thousands of years its people have lived by the sea. More than four thousand years ago, ancient Oman was known as Magan. Its people sold copper to the cities of Mesopotamia. Copper was a very valuable metal because people used it to make tools and weapons.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Later, Oman became famous for another product. This was frankincense, a sweet-smelling resin that comes from trees in Dhofar, in the south. Traders carried it by land and by sea to Egypt, Rome and India. It was very valuable, and many people used it in their temples and homes.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The traders needed good ships. Omani shipbuilders made wooden boats called dhows. They did not use iron nails. Instead, they sewed the wooden planks together with rope made from coconut fibre. Some years ago, a copy of an old ship called the Jewel of Muscat was built in this traditional way, and it sailed from Oman to Singapore.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Sailors also used the seasonal winds, called monsoon winds. In summer the wind blows in one direction, and in winter it changes direction. Sailors waited for the right wind to cross the Indian Ocean to India and to come back home again.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: One of the most important ports was Sohar. It was a rich and busy city more than a thousand years ago, and it is linked to the legend of Sinbad the Sailor. Sailors from Sohar travelled to East Africa and India. Some even sailed as far as China, which was a very long journey.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Trade did more than bring money to Oman. Merchants brought spices, cloth and new ideas from many countries, and they took Omani goods and ideas with them. Because of this, Oman became a meeting place for different cultures.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Today, the sea is still important to Oman. Many people work in ports, and visitors can see traditional dhows in places like Muscat and Sur. These beautiful boats remind us of the proud sea history of our country.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Thank you for listening.

short.q: Which metal did ancient Oman sell to Mesopotamia?
Which sweet-smelling product comes from trees in Dhofar?
What did shipbuilders use to sew the planks together?
Which port is linked to the legend of Sinbad the Sailor?

tf.statement: Dhow builders used iron nails to join the planks.

reading1.title: The Story of the Internet
passage: Today, it is hard to imagine life without the internet. We use it every day to study, to talk to friends, to watch videos and to shop. More than five billion people around the world are now online. However, the internet is not very old, and its story began more than fifty years ago.

In the 1960s, scientists in the United States wanted computers in different places to share information. They built a small network called ARPANET. In 1969, the first message was sent from one computer to another. Only two letters were sent before the system stopped working. Still, the test showed that the idea was possible.

In 1971, an engineer named Ray Tomlinson sent the first email between two computers. He chose the @ symbol to separate the name of the user from the name of the computer. Email quickly became popular with scientists and universities.

The internet became much easier to use because of the World Wide Web. It was invented by a British scientist, Tim Berners-Lee, in 1989, while he was working at CERN in Switzerland. People often think that the web and the internet are the same, but the web is only one service that runs on the internet. In 1991, the first website went online.

In the 1990s, home computers became cheaper, and many families connected to the internet by telephone lines. Search engines helped people to find information, and the first online shops appeared. After the year 2000, faster connections made it possible to watch videos and listen to music online. Smartphones, which became popular after 2007, put the internet in everyone's pocket.

The internet has brought many benefits. Students can learn from teachers in other countries, and companies can sell their products all over the world. However, there are also problems, such as fake news, cyber bullying and too much screen time. Experts say that we should learn to use the internet wisely, protect our personal information and take regular breaks from our screens.

What happened to the first message in 1969?

The system stopped before it finished.

To show the time of the message

options: It is exactly the same as the internet.
It is one service that runs on the internet.

reading2.title: Energy from the Earth
passage: Geothermal energy is the heat that comes from inside the Earth. The word geothermal comes from two Greek words: geo, which means Earth, and therme, which means heat. The Earth is like a giant ball of hot rock. At the centre, the temperature is thousands of degrees, and some of this heat slowly moves up towards the surface.

In some places, this heat is easy to see. Hot springs, geysers and volcanoes are all signs of heat under the ground. People have used hot springs for bathing for thousands of years. In Oman, there are hot springs near Rustaq and Nakhal, and many visitors enjoy them.

To produce electricity, engineers drill deep wells into the ground until they reach very hot water or steam. The steam rises to the surface through pipes and turns a turbine. The turbine drives a generator, which makes electricity. After that, the water is cooled and sent back underground so that it can be heated again.

Geothermal energy has several advantages. First, it is clean because it produces very little pollution compared with coal or gas. Second, it is reliable. Solar panels need sunshine and wind turbines need wind, but the heat under the ground is always there, day and night, in every season. Third, a geothermal power station does not need a large area of land.

Iceland is a good example of a country that uses this energy well. Because it has many volcanoes and hot springs, most of its homes are heated with geothermal hot water. Geothermal power also gives Iceland a large part of its electricity.

However, geothermal energy has some disadvantages. Power stations can only be built in places where hot rocks are close to the surface. Drilling deep wells is very expensive, and sometimes small amounts of gas can escape from under the ground. In addition, there is a small risk of earth tremors near some stations.

Today, geothermal energy supplies only a small part of the world's electricity. However, scientists believe that it has a bright future. New drilling methods may allow more countries to use the heat under their feet.

short.q: What does the word geo mean?
Name one place in Oman where there are hot springs.
What do engineers drill to reach hot water or steam?
Why is geothermal energy reliable? Because ________
short.answer: the heat is always there, day and night / in every season

short.q: Which country heats most of its homes with geothermal hot water?

chart.title: Energy-Saving Habits of Families in One Town
chart.model:
The bar chart shows energy-saving habits in 2020 and 2024. The energy-saving habits were switching off lights, using led bulbs, closing curtains and using solar heaters. Overall, switching off lights was most popular in 2020, whereas using LED bulbs was most popular in 2024.
Firstly, the most popular habit in 2020 was switching off lights, with 60% of families. This was followed by using LED bulbs (30%) and closing curtains (15%). However, the least popular habit in 2020 was using solar heaters, with only 5% of families.
In contrast, the most popular habit in 2024 was using LED bulbs, with 70% of families. This was followed by switching off lights (65%) and closing curtains (40%). However, the least popular habit in 2024 was using solar heaters, with only 35% of families.
To summarize, switching off lights was popular in both years. However, the biggest difference was in using LED bulbs, where 30% chose it in 2020, whereas 70% did in 2024.

email.situation: Imagine you are Sultan, a student at your school. The school pays a lot of money for electricity every month.
email.task: Write a formal email to your principal, Mr Hamdan, and suggest installing solar panels at the school. In your email, write about:
bullets: why solar panels would be useful
where the panels could be placed
how the school could pay for them
email.model:
Dear Mr Hamdan,

I hope this email finds you in good health and high spirits. I am writing this email to recommend installing solar panels at our school.

First, solar panels would save the school a lot of money on electricity. For example, the air conditioners use much power every day. Moreover, solar energy is clean and helps to protect the environment.

Second, the panels could be placed on the roof of the main building, because it gets strong sunshine. Moreover, the school could pay for them with help from parents and local companies. Therefore, the cost would be small.

Thank you for your time and attention. I look forward to your response. Please let me know if you need any further information.

Yours sincerely,
Sultan
